Khan Yunis Massacre

Massacre · 1956-11-03 · During Israeli occupation of Gaza in Suez Crisis

3-12 Nov 1956
Date
Khan Yunis, Gaza
Historical Location
275-525
Deaths
Multiple sites
Mass Graves
Location, thenKhan Yunis (Khān Yūnis), Egyptian-administered Gaza Strip
Location, nowKhan Yunis, Gaza Strip, Palestine; Major city; heavily damaged in 2023-2024 conflict
PerpetratorsIsrael Defense Forces; IDF Intelligence units; Shin Bet security forces
ClassificationWar Crime; Crimes Against Humanity (UNRWA/UN GA Doc A/3512)

Summary

In October-November 1956, Israel launched Operation Kadesh in coordination with France and the UK's invasion of Egypt during the Suez Crisis. Israeli forces rapidly occupied the Gaza Strip and Sinai Peninsula. During the occupation of Gaza, IDF conducted systematic 'screening' operations ostensibly to identify Egyptian soldiers and Palestinian fighters (fedayeen) who had infiltrated Israel.

On November 3, 1956, in Khan Yunis and its refugee camp, Israeli forces conducted mass roundups of male residents. During screenings, curfews, and arbitrary detentions, IDF personnel systematically executed civilians. UNRWA Director for Gaza Affairs compiled detailed victim lists and reported to UN General Assembly that 275 men were killed in Khan Yunis and 111 in nearby Rafah. Palestinian sources documented 415 killed with 57 missing. Methods included shooting during curfew, execution after screening, and arbitrary killings.

Bodies were buried in mass graves, including in the streets of Khan Yunis. UNRWA provided names, ages, and circumstances of death for verified victims. Despite international documentation and UN reports, no Israeli personnel were prosecuted. Israel withdrew from Gaza in March 1957 under international pressure, particularly from the United States and Soviet Union.

Timeline

1956-10-29 00:00:00 Operation Kadesh beginsIsrael launches invasion of Sinai Peninsula in coordination with Franco-British attack on Egypt. Part of coordinated Suez Crisis military operations. — UN Security Council Records 1956
1956-11-02 00:00:00 IDF occupies Gaza StripIsraeli forces complete occupation of Gaza Strip and Khan Yunis. Begin imposing military administration and curfews. — UNRWA Historical Records
1956-11-03 00:00:00 Khan Yunis massacre beginsIDF conducts mass screenings of male residents in Khan Yunis and refugee camp. Systematic executions begin. Men rounded up for 'identification' of fedayeen and Egyptian soldiers. — UNRWA Special Report A/3512
3-12 November Systematic killingsOver 10 days, IDF personnel shoot civilians during curfew, execute detainees after screenings, conduct arbitrary killings. Bodies buried in streets and mass graves. UNRWA documents 275 deaths in Khan Yunis. — UNRWA Director Report, December 15, 1956
1956-11-12 00:00:00 Rafah massacreSeparate mass killing in nearby Rafah refugee camp. UNRWA documents 111 deaths. Similar pattern of screenings and executions. — UNRWA Special Report
1956-12-15 00:00:00 UNRWA report submittedUNRWA Director for Gaza Affairs submits detailed report to UN General Assembly (Document A/3512) documenting 275 deaths in Khan Yunis, 111 in Rafah, with names, ages, and circumstances. — UN General Assembly Official Records - 11th Session
1957-03-01 00:00:00 Israeli withdrawalUnder intense US and Soviet pressure, Israel withdraws from Gaza Strip and Sinai. UNEF (UN Emergency Force) deployed. No accountability for massacres. — UN Security Council Records

Testimony

UNRWA Director, Gaza AffairsSubmitted detailed report to UN General Assembly December 15, 1956 (Document A/3512): 'During the period 3-12 November 1956, 275 persons were killed in Khan Yunis and its refugee camp.' Report included names, ages, circumstances of death compiled from credible witness accounts and physical evidence. — UNRWA Special Report, UN GAOR 11th Session, Annexes, Agenda Item 66, Document A/3512
Benny MorrisIn 'Israel's Border Wars 1949-1956': 'Israeli troops...massacred, apparently in cold blood, some 275 Palestinian civilians in Khan Yunis...and another 111 Palestinians in Rafah.' Based on Israeli military archives and UNRWA documentation. Confirmed systematic nature of killings. — Israel's Border Wars 1949-1956' (Oxford University Press, 1993)
Avi ShlaimIn 'The Iron Wall': 'In Khan Yunis and Rafah, IDF units committed what can only be described as war crimes.' Documented that killings occurred during screenings ostensibly to identify fedayeen but resulted in mass civilian deaths. — The Iron Wall: Israel and the Arab World' (W.W. Norton, 2000)
International Committee of the Red CrossICRC delegates present in Gaza after Israeli withdrawal documented mass grave sites and interviewed survivors. Reports submitted to UN detailed systematic nature of killings and burial procedures. — ICRC Reports to UN, 1956-1957
Palestinian SurvivorsSurvivors described IDF soldiers rounding up men for 'identification checks,' taking them away, and returning without them. Bodies found later in mass graves. Families heard gunshots during screenings. Men shot for curfew violations or arbitrary reasons. — Palestinian oral histories; documented by PCBS

War crimes

Systematic Screenings and ExecutionsIDF conducted mass roundups of male residents for 'screening' to identify fedayeen and Egyptian soldiers. During and after screenings, soldiers systematically executed civilians. UNRWA documented names and circumstances of 275 killed in Khan Yunis alone. — UNRWA Report A/3512
Curfew KillingsStrict curfews imposed; civilians shot on sight for violations. Many killed for minor infractions or misunderstandings. UNRWA documented multiple cases of civilians shot during curfew hours. — UNRWA Documentation
Mass GravesBodies buried in mass graves including in streets of Khan Yunis. Hasty burials prevented proper identification of all victims. Some bodies left exposed for days as warnings. — ICRC Reports 1956-57
Arbitrary Detentions and KillingsMass arbitrary arrests during occupation. Detainees held without charge; many executed without trial or due process. No military tribunals or legal proceedings documented. — UN Documentation
Collective PunishmentEntire neighborhoods and refugee camp subjected to collective punishment. Punitive measures included mass killings, curfews, house demolitions for suspected resistance or fedayeen activity.

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 3 (Common Article): Prohibits violence to life and person, murder, cruel treatment, torture. Systematic executions violated core protections even during armed conflict.
Customary International Humanitarian LawDistinction principle: Failed to distinguish between combatants and civilians during screenings. Executed civilians arbitrarily.
Modern ClassificationUnder Rome Statute of International Criminal Court: acts would constitute crimes against humanity (murder, extermination) and war crimes (willful killing of protected persons, murder).
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 27: Protected persons entitled to respect for persons, honor, family rights. Shall be protected against violence. Mass killings violated fundamental protections.
Customary International Humanitarian LawProhibition of arbitrary deprivation of liberty: Mass arbitrary detentions without due process violated customary law.
Modern ClassificationSystematic nature of killings over 10-day period suggests crimes against humanity element of widespread or systematic attack against civilian population.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 32: Prohibited physical suffering or extermination of protected persons. Screenings followed by executions constituted extermination.
Customary International Humanitarian LawProhibition of collective punishment: Entire populations of Khan Yunis and Rafah subjected to collective punishment for suspected fedayeen presence.
Fourth Geneva Convention (1949) ViolationsArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): Willful killing of protected persons constitutes grave breach (war crime). Mass executions in Khan Yunis and Rafah were grave breaches.

Commanders

1915-1981 Moshe DayanOverall command of IDF operations during Suez Crisis including Operation Kadesh. Oversaw Gaza Strip occupation and screening procedures that led to mass killings in Khan Yunis and Rafah. Later Defense Minister (1967, 1969-74). Never prosecuted for 1956 Gaza operations.
1886-1973 David Ben-GurionOrdered Operation Kadesh in coordination with France and UK during Suez Crisis. Authorized occupation of Gaza Strip. Made final decisions on military operations in Khan Yunis and Rafah. Oversaw policies during occupation period.
1911-2003 Moshe CarmelCommander of Israeli forces occupying Gaza Strip. Directly responsible for ground operations including screening procedures, curfews, and security operations in Khan Yunis and Rafah that resulted in mass civilian deaths.
1923-2016 Shimon PeresKey architect of Israel's alliance with France and UK for Suez operation. Facilitated military coordination. Later Prime Minister and President. Never faced accountability for role in 1956 Gaza operations.
